text:
sarah: heads-up — canary jobs in ap-southeast1 started hitting intermittent allreduce hangs after the NCCL 2.27 bump. A100 inference pools. Observed socket flaps + repeated `ncclCommDestroy` in the traces.

jamal: which canary job ids? any common kernel+driver combo across failures?

sarah: canary ids: ci-infer-237, ci-infer-241. Both on cuda 12.2 / driver 540.x, kernel 6.1. Logs show repeated timeouts during allreduce and a spiky `socket` error around the same time. Snippet:```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] nccl: WARN Allreduce timeout on rank 0
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] nccl: ERROR socket read failed: TLS: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] nccl: fatal error, aborting
```

liam: hmm. that pattern smells like P2P/IB fallback thrash + kernel network scheduling. Can you try forcing socket transport to see if it stabilizes? e.g. set `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` or `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` on the canary runtime.

marta: we rolled one of the test pools back to nccl 2.26 this morning — zero hangs in the same window. Canary with 2.27 had 4/20 failures in the hour.

ops-bot: canary-check: ap-southeast1 canary group: 4 failures / 20 runs in last 1h. Alerting on error-rate > 10%.

anita: operational impact: if we force-socket fallback at runtime we see ~18-25% throughput drop on large-batch inference (higher cost), but it avoids hangs. Short-term tradeoff vs rollback.

ryan: what about kernel/driver interactions? vendor notes about 540.x + 6.1 had a NIC IRQ coalescing edge case with large RDMA transfers. Could be surfacing via NCCL collective patterns.

jamal: action proposal: 1) apply `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` on canary fleet to stabilize, 2) roll back critical serving pools to nccl 2.26 where SLA-sensitive traffic runs, 3) open escalation with HW vendor for driver+kernel trace correlation, 4) schedule a controlled test matrix (2.26/2.27 x 540.x x kernel 6.1/5.15) in a mixed-arch rack.

sarah: implemented (1) on canary at 09:25Z. Immediate reduction in failures — went from 4/20 to 0/20 in 30m. Leaving debug logs enabled and collecting `nccl-tests` allreduce traces.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: nccl 2.26 rollout to serving pools tagged `prod-aus-*` scheduled 09:40Z. Will ramp to 50% over 10m then 100% if green.

marta: please coordinate capacity — rollback + forced-socket increases GPU-hours per query; ops please open cost watch. We may need to throttle batch sizes on non-critical tenants to keep within commitments.

ryan: I'll own vendor escalation and kernel trace correlation. Jamal, can you own the test matrix and perf comparison?

jamal: on it. I'll post the matrix and expected metrics in this thread once ready. Also will add a short doc snippet with env vars to set as mitigation.

sarah: thanks — keeping this thread for timeline. If anyone sees similar in other regions (us-west/eu), ping me.

liam: FYI long-term option: we may prefer a small NCCL patch or different topology selection heuristics rather than permanently forcing socket fallback (to avoid 20% cost hit).

anita: acknowledged. I'll open an internal cost-impact ticket and flag customer SLAs that might be affected.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-032-17 — multicard hang after nccl bump (priority P2). Links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-032-17

sarah: closing loop for now — canary stable after env mitigation + rollback on prod-critical pools. We'll reconvene after vendor analysis. :thumbsup:
